scope: Proposition 7.1 (Contact lower bound) of the manuscript “A directional zero–one law for finite-range-dependent random environments” (preprints/A-directional-zero-one-law-for-finite-range-dependent-random-environments-October-5-2026/directional-zero-one-finite-range.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 220 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 010edc479fd82038), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 30. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Suppose that P0(Ae1 ) > 0 and P0(A−e1 ) > 0, and let m(J) be the contact statistic of the opposed tapes defined in (4.8). There are constants c > 0 and an integer c1 ≥ 0 such that, for all sufficiently large integers J, m(J + c1) ≥ cJ 1 + log log J . (7.1)
